report:
Antecedentes Clínicos:
Dolor patelofemoral.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
El menisco lateral es de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura. Aumento de señal del
meniscocapsular del cuerno posterior y parte del cuerpo del menisco medial sin criterios categóricos de
rotura.
Condropatía superficial de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial. El resto de los
cartílagos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones. Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de
distribución difusa de la rótula.
Leve aumento de señal del aspecto superoexterno de la grasa de Hoffa.
Mínimo derrame articular. Pequeño quiste poplíteo polilobulado, con probable filtración con líquido
perifascial hacia cefálico.
Aumento de señal del tercio proximal del tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura. Tendón cuadricipital,
tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Edema del tejido celular subcutáneo del aspecto anterior de la rodilla sin colecciones líquidas categóricas.
Impresión:
Condropatía superficial de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial.
Condropatía con lesiones grado 2 de la rótula de distribución difusa.
Leves signos de un síndrome de hiperpresión externa de la rótula. Mínimo derrame articular. Quiste poplíteo
con probable filtración hacia cefálico.
Tendinosis rotuliana proximal.
Discreto edema del tejido celular subcutáneo del aspecto anterior de la rodilla sin colecciones líquidas
categóricas

The study reveals mild subcutaneous tissue swelling at anterior aspect of the knee.  
 Normal knee joint alignment, no definite fracture or bone contusion is noted.  
  
   Thickened hyperintense PCL with split longitudinal hyperintense from proximal to the distal part. 
 Normal course with preserved signal of ACL is observed.   
   MIld hyperintense proximal MCL is noted.   Medial meniscus is not torn. 
   Mild hyperintense proximal FCL and popliteus tendon are observed.   The biceps femoris tendon is intact. Lateral meniscus is not torn.  
  The PF joint is preserved.  
  No definite osteochondral lesion is observed.  
  Quadriceps and patellar tendons are  intact.  
   Minimal joint effusion, minimal  suprapatellar bursal fluid with mild thickened synovial tissue are noted. 
  Loculated, mild mild septated fluid , about 1.1cm., along posterior medial knee capsule, probably synovial cyst.    High grade, partially torn PCL . 
    Proxima MCL sprain 
   Proximal FCL sprain, popliteus tendon strain 
   Reactive knee synovitis and suprapatellar bursitis 
   Probably synovial cyst at posterior medial knee capsule

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Small joint effusion. No popliteal cyst.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Grade 3 (complete disruption) injury of the distal medial collateral ligament noted. The mid and proximal collateral ligament is thickened with intrinsic high signal abnormality. There is extensive periligamentous edema.

There is some blunting and fraying of the free edge of the body of the medial meniscus suggestive of a small radial tear or defect.

The articular cartilage is unremarkable.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
The articular cartilage is unremarkable. The lateral meniscus and lateral collateral ligament complex appear normal.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
High-grade partial, functionally complete or complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Mild diffuse chondropathy is noted with superficial fraying noted on both sides of the joint, best appreciated at the median ridge of the patellar articular cartilage and in the trochlear groove. At the lateral trochlea however, there are focal areas of high-grade fissuring and delamination.

Bones:
There is a tiny subchondral impaction fracture at the posterolateral aspect of the lateral tibial plateau with associated moderate bone marrow edema.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:

1.There is a tiny subchondral impaction fracture at the posterolateral aspect of the lateral tibial plateau.
2.Grade 3 injury of the medial collateral ligament noted with complete disruption distally.
3.High-grade partial, functionally complete or complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
4.Patellofemoral chondropathy with high-grade fissuring and delamination noted involving the lateral trochlea as detailed above.
5.There is some blunting and fraying of the free edge of the body of the medial meniscus suggestive of a small radial tear or defect.

In the medial compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury.  
 The lateral compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury.  
 The patellofemoral joint, the patellar and trochlear cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. There is subchondral bone marrow edema at the lateral patellar facet (inferior pole). The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact  
 In the intercondylar notch, the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact There is no tibial translation.  
 The medial collateral ligament complexes are intact The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact  
 The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact The popliteofibular ligament is intact The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 No knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion.  Subchondral bone marrow edema at the lateral patellar facet (inferior pole). 
  No MR evidence of cartilage, meniscus and ligament abnormalities.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication:  Knee pain.. 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar and multisequence MRI of the right  knee without IV contrast.   

FINDINGS: 

JOINT EFFUSION:  Moderate knee joint effusion. Small popliteal cyst. 

ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

POSTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

MEDIAL MENISCUS: Intact. 

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:  Within normal limits. 

LATERAL MENISCUS:  Diminutive appearance of the posterior body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus suggestive of large radial tear in the absence of previous meniscectomy.

The meniscal body also demonstrates complex tearing involving the free edge and the undersurface.

Intrasubstance degeneration in the anterior horn. 

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:  High-grade and full-thickness cartilage loss involving the central to posterior aspects of the femoral condyle and tibial plateau, with mild subchondral edema. Small central and marginal osteophytes. 

MEDIAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT:  Intact.

LATERAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT COMPLEX:  Intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT: Diffuse mild thinning of the patellar cartilage. There is high-grade and full-thickness cartilage loss throughout the trochlea, maximal centrally and laterally, with multifocal subchondral bone marrow edema. 

EXTENSOR APPARATUS:  Quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. 

BONE MARROW:  No fracture. 
 
OTHER:  None. 


IMPRESSION:

1. Diminutive appearance of the posterior body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus, suggestive of large radial tear in the absence of previous meniscectomy.

2. Moderate lateral and patellofemoral compartment osteoarthritis.

3. Moderate knee joint effusion and small popliteal cyst.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Dolor patelofemoral rodilla derecha.
Hallazgos:
Ligamentos cruzados y colateral lateral sin alteraciones.
Leve engrosamiento de señal intermedia del componente superficial del ligamento colateral medial
en su tercio proximal, sin signos de rotura. El resto de los componentes del complejo ligamentario
medial sin alteraciones.
Leve aumento de señal del meniscocapsular del cuerno posterior del menisco medial que podría
representar una lesión parcial regional.
Menisco lateral de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones. Úlceras
condrales de espesor parcial y prácticamente total de la unión entre la faceta medial y vértice de la
rótula, sin cambios óseos secundarios.
Aumento de señal del aspecto superoexterno de la grasa de Hoffa.
Mínimo derrame articular. No hay quistes poplíteos patológicos.
Leve aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital y de la inserción proximal del
tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura.
Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Discreto edema de un las partes blandas entre la banda iliotibial y el cóndilo femoral lateral que
podrían representar fenómenos de fricción.
Impresión:
Leve engrosamiento que impresiona secuelar del componente superficial del ligamento colateral
medial.
Probable lesión meniscocapsular del cuerno posterior del menisco medial, correlacionar con
clínica.
Condropatía con lesiones grado dos y tres a de la rótula.
Signos de un síndrome de hiperpresión externa de la rótula y de fricción de la banda iliotibial.
Mínimo derrame articular.
Leve tendinosis rotuliana proximal y cuadricipital distal.

> Osteophytes and irregular thining intra-articular cartilage of left knee, reflecting osteoarthritis; Subchondral bone marrow edema/cysts of medial femoral condyle
> Severe wearing of medial facet cartilage of patella, reflecting grade 4 chondromalacia; patellar osteophytes
  Severe wearing of medial femoral trochlea with subchondral edema, reeflecting grade 4 chondromalacia.
> Patellar enthesophyte and tendinosis of quadriceps tendon.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis. Retrocondylar bursitis; popliteal bursitis
> Linear signal intensity in medial and lateral meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of grade 2 intrasubstance signal, maybe due to degeneration.
  Increased singal intensity of meniscocapsular junction posterior horn of medial meniscus
> The contour of ACL in a straight line and increase interstitial signal intensity inside on F/S T2WI, in favor of mucoid degeneration.
> Mild interstitial increased signal of PCL and lateral patellar retinaculum, in favor of grade 1 injury or degeneraiton.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Increased fat stranding and minimal fluid accumulation located along the pes anserinus, R/O Anserine bursitis
> Subcutanoeus edema over left knee
> In favor of focal fatty muscle transformation of gastrocnemius muscle. Mild muscle edema also noted.
> Some varicose veins.
Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee, more severe at meidal compartment of left knee and grade 4 chondromalacia of patellofemoral joint and 3-4 chondromalacia of medial femorotibial joint.
2. Synovitis of left knee and suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae; prominent retrocondylar bursitis and popliteal bursitis. 
3. Anserine bursitis.
4. Degeneration of meniscus and R/O Ramp lesion over meniscocapsular junction of posteiror horn of medial meniscus.
5. In favor of mucoid degeneration of ACL.R/O grade 1 injury or degeneraiton of PCL and lateral patellar retinaculum.
6. Subcutanoeus edema over left knee.Some varicose veins.
7. Mild subcutanoeus edmea and muscle edema over left knee.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

 The lateral compartment, there is probable small horizontal tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The patellofemoral joint, the patellar and trochlear cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 In the intercondylar notch, there is complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.  
 The medial and lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Minimal amount of left knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is bone bruise at mid weight-baring lateral femoral condyle and posterolateral tibial plateau.   - Horizontal oblique tear at the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus.  
 - Probable small horizontal tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. 
 - Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance.

Kleines Kontusionsödem am anteromedialen Femurcondylus (Serie 7/ Image 15). Ansonsten regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Intakter Knorpel. Radiärer Riss des Innenmeniskushinterhorns mit vertikaler Rissbildung in der Pars intermedia (Serie 3/ Image 112, Serie 7/ Image 22). Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Intakter Knorpel. Intakter Außenmeniskus. Intaktes LCL.

Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Bis nach subchondral reichender Knorpeldefekt der medialen Patellafacette (Outerbridge Grad 4) (Serie 3/ Image 56, Serie 8/ Image 27). Regelrechte Darstellung des Lig. patellae. Intakte Quadrizepssehne. Regelrechter Hoffa`scher Fettkörper.

Intakte Kreuzbänder. Mehrere, unspezifische kleine Zysten am Ansatz des HKB im posterioren Tibiaplateau (Serie 9/ Image 17).
